en.title: Minimum Chairs
en.description:
Given the arrival times S[i] and departure times E[i] of n guests, compute the maximum number of guests who need seats at the same moment during the whole event. Treat each stay as the half-open interval [S[i], E[i]): a guest who leaves at time t has already freed their seat, so a departure and an arrival at the same moment can reuse the same chair.

This site's valid input ranges: 1≤n≤200000; all times are integers, -10^9≤S[i]<E[i]≤10^9. These ranges are added by this site and are not claimed to come from OAMaster; the original statement published no constraints.

Original source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/google#45-minimum-number-of-chairs (fixed OAMaster snapshot fingerprint eb24ff834abb2e8ef515db29a91308414307144aad15804f989d63e249731470). Supporting evidence for the same problem: https://leetcode.com/discuss/post/356520/google-oa-2019-min-number-of-chairs/; endpoint convention: https://www.fastprep.io/problems/google-meeting-rooms-ii.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line gives n arrival times S[i]; the third line gives the corresponding n departure times E[i].
en.output: Output the maximum number of guests present at the same time during the event, which is the minimum number of chairs required.
en.explanation: Record an arrival as +1 and a departure as -1; at the same moment, process departures before arrivals, and scan for the maximum headcount.
hints: Treat each arrival and each departure as a time event.
Half-open intervals require departures to be processed before arrivals at the same moment.
